PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Gestational Age: 22 weeks
Sample Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal screening for chromosomal trisomies at 22 weeks gestation

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniotic fluid cells using chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers. Multiple informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S858, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1446

Fluorescent PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis. Peak area ratios were calculated for each informative marker. Normal diallelic ratios range from 0.8-1.4. Triallelic patterns or skewed ratios (>1.8 or <0.65) indicate trisomy.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: NORMAL
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns with ratios within normal range
D13S631: 1.02
D13S258: 0.94
D13S742: 1.11
D13S628: 0.89

Chromosome 18: NORMAL
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns with ratios within normal range
D18S535: 1.08
D18S391: 0.91
D18S858: 1.13
D18S386: 0.96

Chromosome 21: NORMAL
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns with ratios within normal range
D21S1435: 0.87
D21S1411: 1.09
D21S1412: 0.95
D21S1446: 1.04

CONCLUSION
Normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormality detected.

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a normal pattern for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21, indicating the absence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this fetal sample.

LIMITATIONS
1. This test does not exclude the possibility of maternal cell contamination. However, the presence of biallelic patterns suggests fetal origin of the sample.
2. Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected by this methodology.
3. This test does not detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements, microdeletions, or segmental imbalances.
4. This test is limited to chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 and does not assess other chromosomes.
5. Uniparental disomy cannot be excluded by this test.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Follow-up testing to be performed by the cytogenetics laboratory, including full karyotype analysis, to provide comprehensive chromosomal assessment. This will detect abnormalities not covered by QF-PCR screening.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted name] Medical Center Clinical Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
